scope: BPI rule application receipt transaction visibility, restart replay, idempotency, terminal-state protection and DLQ acceptance

phases.name: listenerRestartExactReplay
phases.expected: exact redelivery keeps revision 2; inbox 1; audit 1

phases.name: committedApplied
phases.expected: APPLIED revision 3; inbox 2; audit 2; rejection error cleared

phases.name: staleRejectedAfterApplied
phases.expected: inbox records the distinct event while APPLIED revision 3 and audit count 2 remain unchanged

phases.name: poisonPayloadDeadLetter
phases.expected: original bytes and source-topic DLT header reach the DLQ; no business inbox mutation

verificationSql: SELECT application_status, application_deployment_id, revision, application_error_code FROM bpi.bpi_outbox_events WHERE tenant_id = :tenant AND id = :publication_id;
SELECT count(*) FROM bpi.bpi_inbox_events WHERE tenant_id = :tenant;
SELECT action, before_revision, after_revision FROM bpi.bpi_audit_events WHERE tenant_id = :tenant AND object_id = :publication_id ORDER BY after_revision;
limitations: Embedded Kafka is real broker protocol execution but is not the target Kafka cluster.
A transactional Kafka producer emulates the Flink checkpoint sink; this does not prove that the deployed Flink job emits the receipt after a successful checkpoint.
The acceptance does not cover a browser-to-Java-to-Kafka/Flink round trip.
The acceptance does not claim target test-environment deployment or production readiness.
